category: Filters III - Filter Gallery effects (Artistic, Brush Strokes, Sketch)
description: The individual effects hosted by Filter > Filter Gallery, one entry each with the exact slider ranges. All of them need an 8-bit RGB, Grayscale or Duotone document, can be stacked as effect layers inside the gallery, and (except Diffuse Glow, Glass, Ocean Ripple and Texture Fill) are not exposed in the ExtendScript DOM - record them with ScriptingListener or apply them through a Smart Object so they remain editable.

tools.name: Colored Pencil
tools.description: Redraws the image as crosshatched coloured-pencil strokes on a paper whose colour is the current background swatch, leaving flatter areas as paper showing through. Set the background colour before opening the gallery to control the paper tone.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Colored Pencil
tools.example:
1. Set the background colour to a warm cream.
2. Filter > Convert for Smart Filters, then Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Colored Pencil: Width 4, Pressure 8, Paper Brightness 25.
tools.notes: 8-bit RGB/Grayscale only. Uses the background colour, so record it in an action with a Set Background Color step.

tools.name: Cutout
tools.description: Reduces the image to a small number of flat colour levels with simplified edges, like layered cut paper or a screen-printed poster. The most useful gallery filter for vector-style illustration and for preparing images to trace.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Cutout

parameters.name: Edge Fidelity
parameters.description: 1-3; how closely edges follow the original.

tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Cutout: Levels 4, Simplicity 4, Fidelity 2 - then Image > Adjustments > Posterize is unnecessary because Cutout already quantises the colours.
tools.notes: Works well with Poster Edges stacked on top as a second effect layer.

tools.name: Dry Brush
tools.description: Paints the image with a dry-brush technique that simplifies colour into ranges while keeping edges crisp, somewhere between oil and watercolour. One of the most natural-looking painterly gallery filters.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Dry Brush
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Dry Brush: Size 2, Detail 8, Texture 1 for a subtle painted look that survives printing.
tools.notes: For larger canvases the strokes look small; downsample a copy, apply, then upsample if you want bold strokes.

tools.name: Film Grain
tools.description: Adds an even grain pattern to the shadows and midtones and a smoother, more saturated pattern to the highlights, mimicking pushed film. Useful for unifying composited elements and for vintage looks.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Film Grain

parameters.name: Highlight Area
parameters.description: 0-20 how much of the tonal range counts as highlight.

tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Film Grain: Grain 4, Highlight Area 8, Intensity 10 on a Smart Object, then fade the Smart Filter to 60 %.
tools.notes: Filter > Noise > Add Noise (Gaussian, Monochromatic) or the Grain adjustment layer (27.3+) are the non-gallery alternatives.

tools.name: Fresco
tools.description: Paints the image in short, rounded, hastily applied dabs with a coarse texture, imitating wet-plaster fresco. Darker and rougher than Dry Brush.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Fresco
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Fresco: Size 2, Detail 8, Texture 1.
tools.notes: Tends to darken the image; follow with a Levels adjustment.

tools.name: Neon Glow
tools.description: Recolours the image into a two-tone image using the foreground and background colours and adds a glow of a third, chosen colour around the edges. Set foreground/background to dark and light values for the classic neon-tube look.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Neon Glow

parameters.name: Glow Color
parameters.description: Click the swatch to pick the glow colour.

tools.example: Foreground black, background white, Filter Gallery > Artistic > Neon Glow: Size 5, Brightness 15, Glow Color magenta.
tools.notes: Depends on the foreground/background swatches; document them when recording an action.

tools.name: Paint Daubs
tools.description: Simplifies the image into daubs of paint with six brush types ranging from smooth (Simple) to gritty (Dark Rough) and glittery (Sparkle). The Sharpness slider re-introduces edge definition after the daubs.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Paint Daubs

parameters.name: Brush Type
parameters.description: Simple, Light Rough, Dark Rough, Wide Sharp, Wide Blurry, Sparkle.

tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Paint Daubs: Size 8, Sharpness 7, Brush Type Simple.
tools.notes: Wide Blurry at large sizes is a quick painterly background softener.

tools.name: Palette Knife
tools.description: Flattens detail into broad areas of colour as if paint were spread with a knife, revealing the underlying canvas texture. Best on images with large shapes.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Palette Knife
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Palette Knife: Stroke Size 25, Detail 3, Softness 0 followed by Texture > Texturizer (Canvas).
tools.notes: Stack with Texturizer to add the canvas relief the filter implies.

tools.name: Plastic Wrap
tools.description: Coats the image in a shiny plastic film, accentuating surface detail with highlights and shadows as though shrink-wrapped. Frequently used on a duplicate layer set to Overlay to add wet or glossy highlights to liquids and skin.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Plastic Wrap
tools.example:
1. Duplicate layer, Filter Gallery > Artistic > Plastic Wrap: Strength 15, Detail 9, Smoothness 7.
2. Blend mode Overlay, opacity 50 % for glossy water droplets.
tools.notes: Works on any bit depth once converted to 8-bit; try it on a 50 % grey layer with Hard Light for pure highlights.

tools.name: Poster Edges
tools.description: Posterises the colours and draws dark ink lines along the edges, producing a screen-print or comic-book style. The most common companion of Cutout for illustration conversions.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Poster Edges
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Poster Edges: Thickness 2, Intensity 1, Posterization 2.
tools.notes: Edges are drawn in black regardless of swatch colours; reduce Edge Intensity for photographic subjects.

tools.name: Rough Pastels
tools.description: Applies chalky pastel strokes over a textured surface; in bright areas the pastel is thick, in dark areas it is scraped away to reveal the texture. Includes the shared Texture controls (Brick, Burlap, Canvas, Sandstone or a loaded .psd).
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Rough Pastels

parameters.name: Texture / Scaling / Relief / Light / Invert
parameters.description: Texture preset or Load Texture (.psd), Scaling 50-200 %, Relief 0-50, light direction menu, Invert checkbox.

tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Rough Pastels: Length 6, Detail 4, Texture Canvas, Scaling 100 %, Relief 20, Light Bottom.
tools.notes: Any grey-scale .psd can be loaded as a texture; the same texture engine is shared by Underpainting, Conte Crayon, Glass and Texturizer.

tools.name: Smudge Stick
tools.description: Softens the image with short diagonal strokes that smear the darker areas while lightening and losing detail in the highlights, like a pastel rubbed with a finger.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Smudge Stick
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Smudge Stick: Length 2, Highlight Area 0, Intensity 10.
tools.notes: Keep Highlight Area low to preserve bright detail.

tools.name: Sponge
tools.description: Creates images with highly textured areas of contrasting colour, as if sponged paint were dabbed on. Good for foliage and abstract backgrounds.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Sponge
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Sponge: Size 2, Definition 12, Smoothness 5.
tools.notes: Not to be confused with the Sponge tool, which desaturates or saturates by painting.

tools.name: Underpainting
tools.description: Paints the image onto a textured background and then paints the final image over it, giving the loose, blocked-in look of an oil underpainting. Shares the Texture controls with Rough Pastels.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Underpainting
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Underpainting: Brush Size 6, Coverage 16, Texture Canvas, Scaling 100 %, Relief 4.
tools.notes: Often followed by a second effect layer of Paint Daubs for a finished painting.

tools.name: Watercolor
tools.description: Simplifies detail into a medium wet brush and saturates colour where tones change significantly, imitating watercolour pooling. Tends to darken edges strongly; lower Shadow Intensity or fade the filter.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Artistic > Watercolor
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Artistic > Watercolor: Detail 9, Shadow Intensity 1, Texture 1, then Edit > Fade Filter Gallery 70 %.
tools.notes: Real watercolour looks usually combine this with Dry Brush and a paper texture layer in Multiply.

tools.name: Accented Edges
tools.description: Emphasises edges with either chalk-like white strokes (high Edge Brightness) or ink-like black strokes (low Edge Brightness). Between Find Edges and Glowing Edges in strength and fully adjustable.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Accented Edges

parameters.name: Edge Brightness
parameters.description: 0-50; below 25 gives dark ink edges, above gives light chalk edges.

tools.example: Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Accented Edges: Width 2, Brightness 38, Smoothness 5.
tools.notes: 8-bit RGB/Grayscale only.

tools.name: Angled Strokes
tools.description: Repaints the image with diagonal strokes, lighter areas in one direction and darker areas in the opposite direction. Direction Balance shifts how the tones are split.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Angled Strokes
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Angled Strokes: Balance 50, Length 15, Sharpness 3.
tools.notes: Stack with Crosshatch for a full pen-and-ink hatch.

tools.name: Crosshatch
tools.description: Adds pencil-like crosshatching texture while preserving detail and colour, roughening edges. Strength sets how many hatch passes are applied.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Crosshatch
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Crosshatch: Length 9, Sharpness 6, Strength 1.
tools.notes: Desaturate first for a pencil-drawing look.

tools.name: Dark Strokes
tools.description: Paints dark areas with short, tight dark strokes and light areas with long white strokes, boosting contrast dramatically. Useful for gritty, high-key or low-key illustrations.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Dark Strokes
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Dark Strokes: Balance 5, Black 6, White 2.
tools.notes: Strongly darkens; apply on a Smart Object and fade if needed.

tools.name: Ink Outlines
tools.description: Redraws the image with fine narrow lines over the original detail, in the manner of a pen-and-ink drawing with a wash of colour underneath.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Ink Outlines
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Ink Outlines: Length 4, Dark 20, Light 10.
tools.notes: Combine with Cutout beneath it for a coloured-comic style.

tools.name: Spatter
tools.description: Replicates the speckled look of an airbrush spatter, scattering pixels outward. At low radius it is a subtle roughening; at high radius a heavy spray.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Spatter
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Spatter: Radius 10, Smoothness 5 on a text layer converted to a Smart Object for a rough-edged stamp look.
tools.notes: Widely used on masks to roughen an edge: apply to the mask, not the layer.

tools.name: Sprayed Strokes
tools.description: Repaints the image using its dominant colours with angled, sprayed strokes of paint in a chosen direction.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Sprayed Strokes

parameters.name: Stroke Direction
parameters.description: Right Diagonal, Horizontal, Left Diagonal, Vertical.

tools.example: Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Sprayed Strokes: Length 12, Radius 7, Direction Right Diagonal.
tools.notes: Good on backgrounds behind product shots to suggest motion.

tools.name: Sumi-e
tools.description: Paints the image in the Japanese ink-wash style with rich blacks, soft blurred edges and a wet brush loaded with black ink on rice paper.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Sumi-e
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Brush Strokes > Sumi-e: Width 10, Pressure 2, Contrast 16.
tools.notes: Very dark by default; raise Levels afterward or lower Contrast.

tools.name: Bas Relief
tools.description: Transforms the image into a carved low relief lit from one direction, using the foreground colour for dark areas and the background colour for light areas. Set the swatches to black/white for a stone look or to greys for a plaster look.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Bas Relief

parameters.name: Light
parameters.description: Direction menu (Bottom, Bottom Left, Left, Top Left, Top, Top Right, Right, Bottom Right).

tools.example: Press D (black/white), Filter Gallery > Sketch > Bas Relief: Detail 13, Smoothness 3, Light Top Left.
tools.notes: Like all Sketch filters it discards the image colours in favour of the two swatches.

tools.name: Chalk & Charcoal
tools.description: Redraws highlights and midtones as a solid mid-grey background sketched in coarse chalk (background colour) and replaces shadows with black diagonal charcoal lines (foreground colour).
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Chalk & Charcoal
tools.example: Foreground dark brown, background cream, Filter Gallery > Sketch > Chalk & Charcoal: Charcoal 6, Chalk 6, Pressure 1.
tools.notes: Uses both swatches; document them in actions.

tools.name: Charcoal
tools.description: Posterises the image into smeared charcoal strokes: major edges drawn boldly, midtones sketched with diagonal strokes. Charcoal is the foreground colour, paper the background colour.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Charcoal
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Charcoal: Thickness 1, Detail 5, Balance 50.
tools.notes: 8-bit only; convert 16-bit scans first.

tools.name: Chrome
tools.description: Renders the image as a polished liquid-chrome surface, using highlights and shadows as reflection points. Usually followed by Levels or Curves to restore contrast, and the classic basis for chrome text effects.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Chrome
tools.example:
1. Text layer > Rasterize, Gaussian Blur 3 px.
2. Filter Gallery > Sketch > Chrome: Detail 4, Smoothness 7.
3. Curves with a wavy curve for metallic banding.
tools.notes: Discards colour; recolour afterwards with Hue/Saturation (Colorize) or a Gradient Map.

tools.name: Conte Crayon
tools.description: Replicates dense dark and pure white Conte crayons on a textured paper: foreground colour for dark areas, background colour for light areas, with the shared texture engine for the paper.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Conte Crayon
tools.example: Foreground black, background white, Filter Gallery > Sketch > Conte Crayon: Foreground 11, Background 7, Texture Sandstone, Relief 4.
tools.notes: Traditional choice for turning photos into drawings before printing on textured paper.

tools.name: Graphic Pen
tools.description: Uses fine, straight ink strokes in the foreground colour on a paper of the background colour to capture the image, with a stroke direction control. A pen-and-ink stipple/hatch effect.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Graphic Pen

parameters.name: Stroke Direction
parameters.description: Right Diagonal, Horizontal, Left Diagonal, Vertical.

tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Graphic Pen: Length 15, Balance 50, Direction Right Diagonal.
tools.notes: Set black/white swatches for a classic engraving look.

tools.name: Halftone Pattern
tools.description: Simulates a halftone screen (dots, circles or lines) in the foreground/background colours while keeping the tonal range. Faster to control than Color Halftone when a monochrome two-colour screen is wanted.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Halftone Pattern
tools.example: Foreground black, background white, Filter Gallery > Sketch > Halftone Pattern: Size 2, Contrast 5, Type Dot, then set the layer to Multiply over a colour fill.
tools.notes: Line at large Size gives scan-line/CRT effects.

tools.name: Note Paper
tools.description: Makes the image look like handmade paper with the image embossed into it; dark areas appear as holes revealing the background colour. Combines the Emboss and Grain looks.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Note Paper
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Note Paper: Balance 25, Graininess 10, Relief 11.
tools.notes: Uses both swatches for paper and hole colours.

tools.name: Photocopy
tools.description: Imitates a bad photocopy: large dark areas copy only around their edges and midtones fall to solid black or white. Fast way to get a punk-zine or stencil look.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Photocopy
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Photocopy: Detail 7, Darkness 8, then Threshold for a pure stencil.
tools.notes: Foreground = toner colour, background = paper.

tools.name: Plaster
tools.description: Moulds the image in 3D plaster and colours it with the foreground/background swatches; dark areas are raised, light areas sunk. Related to Bas Relief but smoother.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Plaster
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Plaster: Balance 20, Smoothness 2, Light Top.
tools.notes: 8-bit only.

tools.name: Reticulation
tools.description: Simulates the controlled shrinking and distortion of film emulsion, clumping shadows and lightly graining highlights into the two swatch colours.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Reticulation
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Reticulation: Density 12, Foreground 40, Background 5.
tools.notes: Strong effect; fade the Smart Filter for a subtle grain.

tools.name: Stamp
tools.description: Simplifies the image to look like a rubber or wood stamp: pure foreground colour on pure background colour with smoothed edges. The go-to for logo-style silhouettes and two-tone posters.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Stamp
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Stamp: Balance 25, Smoothness 5, then Select > Color Range to lift the black as a selection.
tools.notes: Similar to Threshold but with edge smoothing; works best on high-contrast sources.

tools.name: Torn Edges
tools.description: Reconstructs the image as ragged, torn pieces of paper in the foreground/background colours, useful for high-contrast text and silhouettes.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Torn Edges
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Torn Edges: Balance 25, Smoothness 11, Contrast 17 on a mask to roughen its edge.
tools.notes: Often applied to layer masks rather than pixels.

tools.name: Water Paper
tools.description: Paints the image as blotchy daubs bleeding into fibrous wet paper, blending colours along the paper fibres.
tools.usage: Filter > Filter Gallery > Sketch > Water Paper
tools.example: Filter Gallery > Sketch > Water Paper: Fiber Length 15, Brightness 60, Contrast 80.
tools.notes: Unlike most Sketch filters this one keeps the image colours.
